scope: Itemised queue for the first batch only: Kenya, Vietnam, Peru and Arabic. The seven countries added subsequently (Australia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Nigeria, Philippines, South Africa, Thailand) carry their open items in the verification block at the top of each Markdown file and as todo_verify flags in countries.json; they have not yet been broken out here. Expanding this file to cover them is itself an open task.
note: Each item names what to check and the authority or instrument to check it against. status is 'open' until confirmed against a primary source, at which point record the source and change the field's tag in the Markdown files. The editions field lists which editions carry the item: most are shared, a few are specific to one.

priority_values.high: Wrong value causes an incorrect legal document, a wrong tax amount, or a failed integration.
priority_values.medium: Wrong value causes visible defects or rework but not an invalid document.
priority_values.low: Wrong value causes cosmetic or convenience issues.

Integration modes available for transmitting invoices to the authority.
Required behaviour when the connection to the tax authority is unavailable at the moment of sale, and the permitted catch-up window.
items.note: Determines the offline design. Must be resolved from the regulation, not by engineering preference.

items.item: Taxpayer PIN format and validation rules.

items.item: What the QR code on the printed representation must encode, including field separator format.

items.item: Current official portal URL for each authority named in the file.
Every ESC t code page number, against the specific printer's own command reference.
items.verify_against: target printer command reference, confirmed by printing
items.note: Vendors renumber the code page table; clone firmware diverges while claiming compatibility.

items.item: Whether the target printer performs contextual shaping in firmware or expects pre-shaped presentation forms.
items.verify_against: target printer command reference and a print test
items.note: Per-model fact, not discoverable at runtime. Wrong assumption prints disconnected isolated letters.

items.item: Whether the target printer's ROM font covers the required repertoire, including the lam-alef ligature.
Which digit form is expected on receipts in each target market.
items.verify_against: market convention; sample receipts from the target market
items.note: Market convention, not a technical constraint. Varies by country.

items.item: Currency symbol glyph coverage per market, particularly for symbols added to Unicode recently.
items.note: ROM fonts lag the standard by years. Fall back to the ISO code where coverage is absent.

items.item: Whether any target market imposes legal requirements on receipt language, or on which script tax figures must appear in.
items.verify_against: the tax authority of each target market
